title: The laundromat in heat
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The laundromat in a heat wave: every dryer off, the door propped, the owner at the folding table with a fan, the rack full because nobody comes. Wood comes. The owner says he's the only one. He says he's the only one in January too. She says that's different. It is.

panels.composition: The laundromat, empty, the door propped with a brick, every dryer still, a box fan on the folding table turning slowly. The LAUNDRY owner behind it.

image.prompt: an empty laundromat in heat with its door propped by a brick, every dryer still, and the owner behind a box fan at the folding table, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD in the door with the digests. BARNABY behind him, not coming in from the shade.

image.prompt: a young man in a laundromat doorway holding booklets while a small dog stays outside in the shade, black and white, no words

balloons.text: I'm the only one in January.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner in front of a slow fan, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack, full. Last week's still in it. The fan turning. The strip agrees it's different and can't say how, so it draws the fan.

image.prompt: close on a full wire rack of booklets beside a slowly turning box fan, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'That's different.' It is. The strip draws the fan.
